title: Variable-injectivity of a deduplicated clause
statement: Let $c$ be a clause, that is, a list of literals over the variables $\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$, each literal consisting of a variable together with a negation flag. Form the deduplicated clause obtained from $c$ by keeping, for each variable, only its first occurrence. Then any two literals of this deduplicated clause that share the same variable are in fact the same literal; equivalently, distinct literals of the deduplicated clause have distinct variables.
hypotheses_covered: l₁ belongs to the deduplicated clause
l₂ belongs to the deduplicated clause
l₁ and l₂ have equal variable
replaced:
In $\mathrm{dedupClauseVars}\,c$, any two literals with the same variable are equal;
that is, the resulting clause has pairwise distinct variable indices.
